conviction_note: The fundamental read is a large EPS beat: Q3 had no US hurricane landfall and the cheaper reinsurance program covered the full quarter, so a build from primary documents gives about $1.40-1.80 against a $0.91-1.07 consensus. The reaction read is only modestly positive. HRTG has beaten by 100%+ before, so a beat is the house expectation. Peer UVE crushed estimates on the same reinsurance mechanism and rose only +0.9% the next day. The line that sold this stock in Q1 2026 (-20%), shrinking policies and premiums written, is still shrinking, and Isaias puts a Q4 loss estimate on the call. So p_up is 57 on a 13% abs move (+1.8), while impact_sum is +1.3. The gap is small and both are positive; it is not tidied away.

positioning_check: Short float 3.29%, short ratio (days to cover) 2.75, short interest 0.79m of a 23.89m float; insiders own 19.6%, institutions 65.3% (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=HRTG, read 2026-10-28). The short is not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism on either side. Skew is unavailable: the Nov-20 chain is unusable (ATM spread 154% of mid, total OI 72, put/call OI 0.2) per the sealed baseline, so the option market makes no directional statement. Tape: +5.2% over 20 days and -5.9% over 5 days. The stock rallied from $34.83 on 10-09 (Isaias landfall day) to $37.70 on 10-22, then gave back to about $35.10 intraday 10-28. Over the same days UVE went $48.84 to $46.92, so the pullback is sector-wide, not HRTG-specific (Yahoo chart v8, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HRTG?range=2mo&interval=1d).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 earnings build from primary documents gives about $1.40-1.80 EPS against a $0.91-1.07 consensus. Two inputs drive it. First, Q3 had no US hurricane landfall: Isaias on 2026-10-09 was the first US hurricane since 2024, so it falls in Q4. Second, the 1 June 2026 CAT XOL program costs $367.5m against $430.7m, saving $63.2m a treaty year, or about $15.8m pre-tax a quarter (about $0.40 a share after tax on about 30m diluted shares), and Q3 is the first full quarter of it. The comparable is Q3 2025: $1.63 EPS with zero catastrophe losses, $13.8m net weather, $5.0m favorable prior-year development (PYD) and a 46.1% ceded ratio. Q2 2026 already showed a 42.7% ceded ratio with only one month of the new program. Even with zero PYD and a loss ratio 5-7 points worse than Q3 2025, the build stays above $1.30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats have mostly been bought: Q2 2026 $2.05 vs $0.99 rose +16.47%, Q3 2025 (zero cat, $1.63) rose +12.48%, Q4 2025 rose +17.90% (baseline). The exception is Q1 2026: EPS +20% y/y to $1.19, but the stock fell -20.05%, alongside policies -6.3% and GPW -2.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.91-1.07 is below Q3 2025's $1.63 in a quarter with a lighter reinsurance bill and no landfall. If the street had marked the reinsurance saving and the benign quarter, the FY estimate would be well above $5.38 and the quarter near $1.5. The counter: the stock beat by 107% last quarter, so buy-side expectations are likely above the printed consensus. That is why this is sized well under the 14.5% median reaction.
findings.independence: Supported by different documents. The CAT XOL release (https://investors.heritagepci.com/2026-05-28-Heritage-Announces-Full-Placement-of-2026-2027-CAT-XOL-Reinsurance-Program, 2026-05-28) gives the $367.5m cost and the $50m SE / $38m NE retention. The Q3 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1598665/000119312525267080/d768057dex991.htm) is the comparable. The no-Q3-landfall fact is from https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/catastrophe/isaias-claims-begin-as-panhandle-counts-damage-from-first-us-hurricane-since-2024-593078.aspx (October 2026). Peer UVE's print is filed separately as F2.

findings.finding: Peer Universal Insurance (UVE) reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-22, after Heritage last spoke. GAAP EPS was $1.80 vs $1.38 and adjusted $1.93 vs $1.36. The ceded premium ratio fell 5.1 points to 27.6%, attributed explicitly to the 1 June 2026 reinsurance program, and the net loss ratio fell 5.6 points. That confirms the cheaper-reinsurance mechanism flowing through a Florida homeowners P&L in Q3. Two cautions: UVE's Florida direct premiums written fell 3.3%, and its stock moved only $48.40 to $48.84 (+0.9%) the next session and drifted down about 4% after.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the peer's reaction on the same line: a ~23% EPS surprise driven by cheaper reinsurance bought +0.9% next day (Yahoo UVE daily closes 10-22 48.40, 10-23 48.84, 10-28 ~46.92). HRTG's own reactions to beats are larger (see F1).
findings.why_not_priced: HRTG rose from $36.98 to $37.70 around UVE's print, then fell back below $36, so the read-through has not been bid into HRTG. The peer's muted reaction is the strongest sign that a reinsurance-driven beat is partly expected across the group. That is why this is a small positive and not a second copy of F1.
findings.independence: Different company and different document from F1. It corroborates the mechanism but shares the same driver (the 2026 reinsurance market softening), so it is sized small to avoid counting one fact twice.

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida on 2026-10-09 as a Category 2 (Q4, after the quarter). Florida OIR counted 46,509 claims and $582m of insured losses as of 2026-10-15. Modelers put US private insured losses at $1-4.5bn (Cotality $2-3bn, KCC about $3bn). UVE said claims were 'less significant than initially anticipated'. Heritage's retention under the 2026-27 program is about $50m in the Southeast, before any Osprey Re reduction, which caps Heritage's net hit. Heritage will likely give a Q4 estimate in the release or on the 10-29 call. Against an implied Q4 consensus of about $1.10 ($5.38 FY less $3.23 H1 less about $1.05 Q3), a net retained loss of $15-40m pre-tax ($0.40-1.00 a share) could pull Q4 estimates down.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No HRTG print in this baseline window carried a post-quarter landfall estimate. The tape is the evidence: HRTG rose +8% from landfall day to 10-22, so the market read Isaias as small or inside retention.
findings.why_not_priced: Heritage has not quantified its Panhandle exposure or an Isaias loss, and the OIR exposure tables (https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/southeast/2026/10/08/888368.htm, 2026-10-08) do not list it. If the market had priced a large retained loss, HRTG would not have rallied 8% after landfall. The risk is a number at the top of retention, which would be news. This is macro-to-company transmission with no Heritage confirmation, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Retention figure from the company's 2026-05-28 CAT XOL release (https://investors.heritagepci.com/2026-05-28-Heritage-Announces-Full-Placement-of-2026-2027-CAT-XOL-Reinsurance-Program). UVE's 'less significant than anticipated' comment is from its 10-22 8-K (F2's document). Loss estimates are from https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/catastrophe/cotality-puts-isaias-insured-losses-at-2-billion-to-3-billion-below-prelandfall-estimates-593232.aspx (2026-10-12).

findings.finding: Top line and policy count are still shrinking. Q2 2026: gross premiums written -5.5% to $388.4m, policies in force -5.2% to 350,887, premiums in force -1.4%, commercial residential -12.7% on 'competitive pricing pressure' in Florida. Management said it 'anticipates a return to policy count growth' and that commercial premiums would 'level off in the second half'. Peer UVE's Florida direct premiums written fell 3.3% in Q3, and an Earnings Whispers preview (2026-10-20) is headlined 'Heritage Faces A Tougher Quarter As Reserve-Release Tailwind Fades And Growth Gets Tested'. Q2's $23.4m favorable PYD (about $0.60 a share) is unlikely to repeat at that size. The Q3 test is whether the promised policy-count turn shows up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 is the case: EPS +20% y/y, but policies -6.3% and GPW -2.6% on Florida competition, and the stock fell -20.05%. Q2 2026 GPW was -5.5%, but EPS doubled consensus and the stock rose +16.47%. So a shrinking top line is sold when the EPS beat is not big enough to drown it.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the FY consensus of $5.38 is 14% below 2025's $6.25, so the street models fading reserve releases. It is not priced as an outcome: whether Q3 shows the promised policy-count turn is unknown, and the stock sits only 7.5% below its 52-week high, so a growth disappointment has room to bite. What would differ if fully priced: the stock would trade near Q1's post-print lows, not near the high.
findings.independence: UVE's 10-22 8-K shows Florida direct premiums written -3.3% (different company: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/891166/000089116626000092/a3q26uveex-991xearningspre.htm). The EW preview headline is listed on https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=HRTG. The Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1598665/000119312526212120/hrtg-ex99_1.htm) shows the pattern. Net of the rest of the company: personal residential PIF was +1.2% in Q2 and Q1 new business was +62.7%, which is why this is not sized larger.

findings.finding: Capital return optionality. The quarterly dividend is suspended, with the Board 'reassessing each quarter'. $37.4m remained on the buyback at Q2 plus a new $50m program authorized 2026-05-07; Q2 repurchases were 631,024 shares for $14.6m. Book value per share was $19.09 (+16.5% YTD), so the stock trades at about 1.8x book after a 28.5% ROE quarter. A dividend reinstatement or a stepped-up buyback in the release is possible upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No reinstatement inside the baseline window. The Q1 2026 buyback authorization came alongside a -20% reaction, so a buyback alone has not carried the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Reinstatement is not signalled and is a low-probability event; if the market expected it, the stock would be trading at a dividend-implied premium to peers. It is sized small accordingly.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 release shows the same capital posture (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1598665/000119312526212120/hrtg-ex99_1.htm).

The finding cuts mildly against the 5-day -5.9% pullback, but the pullback is sector-wide (UVE fell from 48.84 to 46.92 over the same days) and sits on top of a +5% 20-day run-up, so the evidence argues for a modest positive only.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (verify the bar): consensus has two sources that disagree ($0.91 finviz vs $1.04 Earnings Whispers). The reported-quarter finding F1 was trimmed from +3.0 to +2.5, not capped harder, because the build clears both bars by more than 25%.

Lesson 1 (a fact is not a reaction): peer UVE's reinsurance-driven beat bought only +0.9%, and HRTG fell 20% on an EPS beat in Q1 2026. p_up moved from 58 to 57; F1 already carried this caveat, so it was not cut again.
Lesson 5 (proxy is small): Isaias F3 left at -0.5, unchanged, as macro-to-company transmission with no Heritage number.
Lessons 8 and 9 checked: abs_move kept at 13 near the 14.5 median; F4 already sized net of personal residential PIF growth. No change.
'A peer's print landing after the company last spoke' (what has worked) supports keeping F2 filed at +0.5.
